# Wine Ops coordinator operating policy

This policy records the user-directed worker, context, and compute workflow.
Apply it to the host coordinator instructions and worker launch prompts; a file
in Git alone does not change a running session. User instructions and enforced
access controls take precedence. Public deployment needs its existing authorization.

## Dispatch and context

- The coordinator assigns games and bounded tasks. Use at most **seven** production
  workers (user update 2026-10-26). Aim for five to seven independent useful tasks when ready
  work exists; do not invent work to fill slots. Serialize shared integration and heavy
  runtime tests. Respect laptop and other agents' ownership.
- Start a fresh worker for each new task; same-task clarification is allowed.
  Workers do not spawn agents or refill the queue.
- Worker automatic compaction is **200,000 total-context tokens**. Coordinator
  compaction is **48,000 tokens of growth after the carried prefix**. These are
  compaction triggers, not spending budgets or instructions to stop a task.
- Verify launcher flags and runtime behavior. On the current host, native child
  spawn inherited the coordinator threshold despite role configuration; use the
  independent `scratch/usage-watch/start-worker.py` launcher until corrected and
  verified. Do not claim config inspection proves runtime inheritance.
- Each task names its exact input revision, owned paths, outcome, relevant tests,
  resource allocation, dependencies, completion notification, and stop condition.
  Runtime tasks must also name the box, expiry, and shutdown owner before launch.

## Wait for outcomes

The worker launcher writes `result.json` and `final.txt`, then queues completion
to the coordinator. `notification.json` records delivery success or failure.

After dispatch, record the worker ID, task, output directory, expected completion
or next check time, and return to an interruptible completion wait. Keep the goal
active while useful work runs. A live worker is not a blocked goal. Do not end
minute-long turns with "still running" and immediately start another goal turn.
Use the host's supported wait mechanism within its tool limits.

- Wake for worker completion, user/Telegram input, a changed dependency, or an
  overdue-worker check. Do not repeatedly reread full logs, source, the backlog,
  disk measurements, or unchanged receipts while waiting.
- If completion delivery is unavailable, use a narrow fallback check no more
  often than every **10 minutes**, unless a task deadline, safety condition, or
  user request requires sooner. Check result existence, notification failure,
  process liveness, and bounded new output before deciding whether to intervene.
- Read Telegram entries after the cursor on wake. Background inbox monitoring
  and the existing watchdog remain enabled; do not create model turns solely to
  read an unchanged cursor.
- Review each result once. Reuse exact-revision evidence already accepted; rerun
  checks when inputs change, evidence is missing, or a specific concern warrants
  it. Independent review should target correctness gaps, not repeat packaging.
- Send status updates for material progress or changed blockers. A queued
  instruction is delivered, not necessarily consumed: require acknowledgement
  before relying on a live worker to change a destructive lifecycle action.

## Test-box lifecycle and build failures

The **coordinator owns shutdown**. A worker must leave its assigned test box
running on completion, a recoverable failure, or handoff, unless its original
task explicitly delegates shutdown or an emergency requires stopping. Include
this rule in the launch prompt rather than correcting it after the task starts.

Keep the same running box through bounded repair and retest when practical.
Before another expensive build, run available cheap prerequisite checks against
the exact candidate; do not call their success a full build or gameplay result.
Record the first real failure, fix that dependency, and retest. Preserve useful
staging and artifacts across handoffs instead of rebuilding the environment.

The coordinator snapshots/stops when work is complete, no useful authorized
follow-up exists, the failure cannot be resolved in the current allocation, or
expiry is imminent. Retain a finite TTL and a shutdown checkpoint; do not leave
compute running indefinitely. Verify actual box state before assigning it.

A denied `sandbox.resume` applies to that operation. Do not retry it unchanged,
alter credentials to evade it, or treat it as evidence that all runtime work is
forbidden. A separately authorized fresh box is a distinct task allocation:
prepare the concrete task first, verify permitted creation/exec, and record its
new identity. Never assume an old access receipt proves current availability.

## Blockers, publication, and efficiency

### Shared local resource-accounting gate (2026-10-23)

Before task-dependent execution, record a measured focused manifest and projected
peak task-owned bytes: checkout/Git data, copied inputs, staging, temporary files,
evidence and outputs, plus growth allowance and an 8 MiB reserve inside the
64 MiB task allocation. Record existing installed executables and read-only donor
inputs separately with identity and standing footprint. Execute installed tools
in place; their pre-existing bytes are not newly staged task bytes. Any new tool
copy, install, extraction or task-created duplicate counts against the allocation.
Do not use links to conceal materialized bytes or double-charge shared standing
inputs. This is disk accounting, not permission to ignore memory/CPU limits.

Require host free space of at least 2,982,150,144 bytes after projected incremental
growth, and retain every mandatory launcher/platform admission control. Record
measured/projected totals, tool identities, command and verdict before execution;
recheck when inputs or allocation change. A denial stops that operation; do not
retry unchanged. Earlier reports using the conflicting installed-Node definition
retain their original qualification limits; this rule does not retroactively
convert them into compliant acceptance evidence. Both active independent reviews
already received this definition in their launch prompts; preserve their progress.

Record each blocker's diagnostic, affected tasks, owner, and observable resume
condition. Keep user holds separate from technical errors. A Git host-key error
needs trusted-host/authentication repair, not a blanket publication ban; retain
strict verification. Existing commit/push/merge authorization still requires
review, relevant checks, current remote-main reconciliation, and verified refs.
Do not force-push shared branches or treat a local commit as remote backup.

The 30-minute usage review should compare concrete outcomes with coordinator
requests, repeated waits, setup retries, and duplicate reviews. Cached input is
a subset of input, not an additional count or free work. Report quota with its
sample time; do not convert a percentage into an invented token balance.

If status-only turns recur, correct waiting behavior immediately. If no eligible
work remains after checking dependencies, record one concise checkpoint and wait
for a dependency/user event; do not repeatedly rebuild the same blocker report.

### Readiness command compatibility checkpoint (2026-10-23)

Make each readiness task's first checkpoint compare all mandatory commands against
its exact authorized execution limits before running the gate sequence. Include
native compilation/instantiation, aggregate live arenas and heap, task-owned staging
and temporary/generated outputs, external launcher capture logs/events and future
growth, and the reserve inside the allocation. Installed tools remain separately
accounted standing inputs. Reuse existing measurements. An incompatible or unknown
requirement stops that operation with a precise evidence-linked allowance request
for coordinator resolution; do not bypass guards or weaken mandatory commands.
Preserve same-task work; no restart or automatic slot refill is implied.

### Shadow Man ABI helper dispatch gate (2026-10-23T06:14 review)

Before dispatching a future Shadow Man build assignment, the coordinator must
retain a passing compatibility receipt for the exact candidate and corrected
static ABI helper. The receipt binds helper hash, candidate/closure identity,
explicit source roots and the complete compiler serialization of both storage
regions and named spans. For candidate b41a7c5f4b752d1f0bdab1141a11d4fed4dc6f9a,
the complete inventory includes DIRECT_WINDOW and must derive
9a3bc9149d58209c; the storage-only b0f1d4c2a339d18f is incompatible.
Require the independent inventory and rejecting omission/change/duplicate tests;
do not substitute the declared fingerprint or weaken payload/signature checks.
Reuse exact-revision passing receipts, invalidate on relevant input/helper change.
The already-running span-static-canonical task owns this correction and its
conditional build; preserve its progress and review its existing receipt on
completion. Do not dispatch another readiness worker or repeat compilation merely
to satisfy this policy. Fresh execution/resource admission remains mandatory.

### Compiler path and excerpt acceptance checkpoint (2026-10-23T07:44 review)

Before a future compiler-dependent acceptance task runs tests, verify the exact
candidate compiler path and Git blob, full-file SHA-256, and the byte-exact
excerpt extraction recipe (line ranges/order, byte count and SHA-256). Bind the
receipt to the helper and candidate revisions. Do not inherit a path, diff
comparison or excerpt assertion from a different revision without checking it.
On a passing checkpoint, continue through acceptance in that same bounded task;
on failure, retain expected/actual identities and the exact mismatch. Routine
owned fixture/path corrections may be completed in the same assignment without
weakening the oracle. Reuse accepted exact-revision receipts when unchanged;
this checkpoint does not require repeating completed acceptance or interrupting
the active native-handler qualification.

### Recovery batch guard checkpoint (2026-10-23T18:18 review)

Before another acquisition batch, verify its actual sequencing wrapper with a
local rejecting metadata/byte-guard fixture and a sentinel download step. Require
the guard's nonzero result to propagate and the sentinel to remain absent; retain
the command and receipt. Do not use a network retry to test this behavior. Each
dependent download/extraction must check its predecessor's exit status and stop
at the first rejection. Already retained archives may be inspected under a fresh
authorized static task without reacquisition. Preserve running assignments;
this checkpoint does not authorize another worker or restart.

### Exact launch configuration checkpoint (2026-10-24T07:23 review)

Before dispatch, the coordinator supplies and verifies the exact trusted Git SSH
configuration and immutable donor revision when checkout is required. Reuse the
retained passing receipt for unchanged configuration; do not replace the dedicated
identity/known-hosts configuration with bare strict SSH or alter trust controls.
Before a conditional guest attempt, validate the actual filename-bearing mount
argv with the canonical parser and enumerate intended files, including commas.
Use supported tree mounts for comma-bearing paths. Continue in the same task on
pass; stop the affected operation on an actual denial or configuration mismatch.
Do not create preparation workers, repeat completed tests or interrupt active
assignments merely to apply this checkpoint. Resource/lifecycle limits remain.

### Pinned artifact pre-dispatch checkpoint (2026-10-24T11:25 review)

Before each worker launch, the coordinator checks that required pinned source
paths exist and match their supplied hashes, or supplies a verified immutable
recovery source with exact revision, paths and hashes. A path from a former
box is not a local input. Retain the check in the dispatch receipt and reuse
it only while those identities remain unchanged. Resolve routine local source
recovery before dispatch; do not launch a preparation worker for this check.
Preserve active same-task progress and existing resource/access controls.

### Scarce validation preflight (2026-10-24T13:55 review)

Before a scarce native/guest acceptance attempt, verify the explicit sparse checkout
and projected publication copies fit the task allocation. Independently check probe
counter-state isolation: use disjoint control addresses, record starting counts, and
reject contamination before consuming the native attempt. Retain historical failures;
reuse accepted exact-revision receipts rather than repeat validation. Check the exact
supervisor limits against every planned artifact, including inherited RLIMIT_FSIZE
versus the selected PNG profile, before staging or guest execution. A mismatch stops
the affected operation; resolve internal configuration within authorization while
preserving actual output, resource, platform and user restrictions. This checkpoint
does not authorize automatic worker refill.

### Runtime deadline preflight (2026-10-24)

Every new guest/native box assignment must have a sibling TASK.runtime.json with one authoritative UTC guestCutoff, handback, shutdown and expiry, optionally createdAt and admissionAt. The launcher validates it before creating an output directory or starting a worker. Prompt times must all belong to that schedule; omit unrelated historical wall-clock times from runtime prompts. Require guestCutoff < handback < shutdown < expiry and an unexpired cutoff. This catches the stale12:28 versus16:55 contradiction locally. Offline tasks need no runtime sidecar. Do not alter a live task or restart work solely for this bookkeeping check.

### Select completion runtime gate (2026-10-24T19:27 review)

Preserve the active lifecycle observer independent review. Before another Maelstrom
runtime assignment, identify and validate an invocation-owned select completion hook
after result storage and before subsequent guest execution/callbacks, covering thunk
and inline CALL/JMP dispatch. Require a positive result observation and rejecting
controls for parked/retried calls, stale EAX and unrelated call identities. Retry
snapshots and return-address/ESP coincidence alone are insufficient. If unavailable,
record the exact source-backed blocker without another capture attempt. Retain fresh
resource admission and validated shutdown schedule. This review does not refill workers.

### Durable acceptance checkpoint (2026-10-26T02:06 review)

After each completed acceptance test group, retain a compact checkpoint recording exact candidate SHA, tested source/fixture hashes, evidence paths and results, remaining checks and blockers. Update atomically after the group completes. Replacement workers reuse exact-revision passing receipts and execute only remaining checks; changed inputs require only affected checks. Keep incidents and first-failure evidence. Do not interrupt active useful work or dispatch a checkpoint-only worker; apply within existing acceptance and at its next completion handoff.

### Consolidated acceptance-to-publication assignment (2026-10-26T07:39 review)

For future fresh integration assignments, combine independent acceptance, affected merged-tree validation, and conditional task-branch/main publication into one bounded task under sole serialized main ownership when prerequisites are ready. Preserve required independent review: rejection stops publication with the unchanged reproducer and repair scope. Attach exact candidate/source/fixture/dependency hashes and reusable passing receipts once; rerun only checks affected by changed inputs. A semantic conflict, resource/access denial, or unavailable main ownership is an explicit gate, not permission to bypass it. Keep durable checkpoints for provider interruptions. Preserve current workers and their scopes; this adjustment does not trigger worker refill or another acceptance of already passed groups.
- `node tools/func-index.js N` / `node tools/dump2png.js LOG --width=N`: name WASM functions / inspect pixels.

**Before adding a console.log to source, check built-in tracing first.** Extend the appropriate runtime tracing wrapper when a primitive is missing; source must stay clean between sessions.

## Detailed references

- [CLI run instructions](docs/cli-run.md): manifests, clocks, calendar/time zone, block budgets, threads and child processes.
- [Tracing](docs/tracing.md): full flag table and how to extend runtime categories.
- [Browser performance and iPhone diagnostics](docs/browser-perf.md): HUD metrics, streaming, evidence limits and real-device tools.
- [Source Parts](docs/source-parts.md): WAT include-order table.
- [JS libraries and rendering surfaces](docs/js-libraries.md): library table and required single back-canvas routing.
- [Tools catalog](docs/tools.md): complete commands, measurement policies and examples.
